Sensitivity of index ranks to construction choices

Source: R/idx.R
idx_sensitivity.Rd

Builds the index many times, each time drawing a normalization, a weighting scheme, and an aggregation method at random, and reports how far each unit's rank moves.

Usage

idx_sensitivity(
  data,
  cols,
  id,
  normalizations = c("z", "minmax", "rank"),
  weightings = c("equal", "dirichlet"),
  aggregations = c("arithmetic", "geometric"),
  n_sims = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  concentration = 1,
  level = 0.9,
  keep_draws = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or sf object with one row per unit.

cols

<tidy-select> Numeric indicator columns to combine.

id

<tidy-select> The column that identifies units. Its values must be unique.

normalizations

Normalization methods to draw from; see idx_normalize().

weightings

Weighting schemes to draw from: "equal", or "dirichlet" for weights drawn from a symmetric Dirichlet distribution with parameter concentration.

aggregations

Aggregation methods to draw from; see idx_combine().

n_sims

Number of draws.

seed

Optional whole number. With a seed the draws are reproducible, and the session's random number stream is restored afterward.

concentration

Parameter of the Dirichlet distribution. The default, 1, draws uniformly from all weight vectors that sum to 1; larger values keep draws closer to equal weights.

level

Coverage of the rank interval.

keep_draws

If TRUE, also return every draw.

Value

If keep_draws = FALSE, a tibble with one row per unit: the id

column, median_rank, and rank_lower and rank_upper, the quantiles bounding the central level share of the unit's ranks. If keep_draws = TRUE, a list with that tibble as summary and a tibble draws with one row per draw and unit: draw, the id column, normalization, weighting, aggregation, index, and rank.

Details

In each draw every option is equally likely, independently of the other choices and of other draws. Rank 1 is the highest index value, and ties share the average rank.

Geometric aggregation needs positive inputs (see idx_combine()), so in draws that use it each normalized indicator is first rescaled linearly to run from 1 to 100. The 100:1 ratio of the endpoints sets how hard the geometric mean penalizes a low value; the absolute scale does not affect ranks. Because z-scores and min-max values are both linear in the raw data, they give identical geometric draws; only rank normalization gives different ones.

See also

idx_normalize(), idx_combine().

Examples

cities <- data.frame(
  city = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
  share = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.6, 0.9),
  isolation = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.8, 0.7)
)
idx_sensitivity(cities, c(share, isolation), id = city,
                n_sims = 200, seed = 1)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   city  median_rank rank_lower rank_upper
#>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 a               4          4          4
#> 2 b               3          3          3
#> 3 c               2          1          2
#> 4 d               1          1          2
